Question: Using NHANES  from 2005 to 2012 we will run a weighted prevalence analysis using exam weights to get the prevalence of clinical relevant depression defined by the following 9 questionnaires: "have little interest in doing things", "feeling down, depressed, or hopeless", "trouble sleeping or sleeping too much", "feeling tired or having little energy", "poor appetite or overeating", "feeling bad about yourself", "trouble concentrating on things", "moving or speaking slowly or too fast", "thought you would be better off dead".  The total score from the nine questions were calculated where each question has value of Not at all (0), Several days (1), More than half the days (2), Nearly every day (3), if value is null assign (0), and the total score >=10 was defined as clinically relevant depression and else was not. We will include people  with T2DM  using the following criteria: self-reported diagnosis of diabetes or “sugar diabetes” at age >=30 years. Exclude participants who initiated  insulin therapy within 1 year of diabetes diagnosis, not pregnant at the time of interview/examination.
Structured Question:
Analysis Type: weighted prevalence (exam)

Dataset: NHANES

Period of Interest: 2005-2012

Inclusion Criteria:
- (self-reported diagnosis of diabetes OR self-reported diagnosis of “sugar diabetes”) AND age >= 30 years

Exclusion Criteria:
- initiated insulin therapy within 1 year of diabetes diagnosis
- pregnant at the time of interview/examination

Grouping Variables: None

Outcome:
- clinical relevant depression = 1 if total score >= 10; 0 otherwise
  total score calculated as the sum of the following 9 questionnaire scores:
    - have little interest in doing things
    - feeling down, depressed, or hopeless
    - trouble sleeping or sleeping too much
    - feeling tired or having little energy
    - poor appetite or overeating
    - feeling bad about yourself
    - trouble concentrating on things
    - moving or speaking slowly or too fast
    - thought you would be better off dead
  Each question's score is mapped as:
    - Not at all: 0
    - Several days: 1
    - More than half the days: 2
    - Nearly every day: 3
  If a question's value is null, assign 0.

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS temp_master_weight;

FROM nhanes.demo_d

-- STEP 3: Create final weight+design table
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS weight_design;
CREATE TABLE weight_design AS
SELECT 
    s.respondent_sequence_number,
    s.masked_variance_pseudo_psu,
    s.masked_variance_pseudo_stratum,
    w.survey_weight
FROM temp_psu_stratum s
INNER JOIN temp_master_weight w
  ON s.respondent_sequence_number = w.respondent_sequence_number;
